# Aratis, the Lawkeeper · Book II, pp. 22–25
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	22
P	Aratis is one of the four main <b>gods</b> (page 178) of Stonetop, the patron god of civilization and records, of laws and wisdom, of order over chaos. Her disciples say that she has been with us since people first stacked stone upon stone and called it home.
P	If one of your initial PCs has the Judge playbook, they will answer many of the questions in this section via their presence, their background, and the decisions they make during character creation and introductions. Defer to that PC as the expert on Aratis in your game, but don't forget to ask other PCs for their opinions and experiences, too.
H2	Themes
HR
P	Choose or roll 1 or 2, and combine.
P	1d12 theme
HR
P	1-2 Civilization/society/settlements
P	3-4 Laws/rules/traditions
P	5-6 Chronicles/record-keeping/writing
P	7 Judgement/arbitration/wisdom
P	8 Cooperation/organization/peace
P	9 Authority/responsibility/duty
P	10 Truth/promises/oaths/honor
P	11 Hospitality/sanctity/generosity
P	12 Defense/resolve/punishment
H2	Questions
HR
P	According to the tales:
Q	How did Aratis come to be (a god)? What's her origin story?
Q	Among which people did the worship of Aratis originate?
Q	Which god is her rival/ally/lover/kin?
Q	What god or demon did she personally defeat/cast out/seal away?
Q	What constellation is tied to Aratis? How so?
Q	Who was the first Judge? What great deed is attributed to them?
Q	What is said to be contained in the Tower Eternal?
P	Use the answers to help decide what Aratis's <b>true nature</b> is (page 180).
H2	Hooks
HR
B	The Judge makes an unpopular ruling; an influential NPC wants them gone.
B	A Judge from another settlement arrives and finds things in Stonetop lacking.
B	A true disciple has a vision of a powerful agent of chaos breaking its bonds.
B	While digging stones or excavating a new foundation, folks in Stonetop discover a long-lost Chronicle of Aratis, sealed and mostly intact.
B	Legend tells of the Tower Eternal, made of <b>black iron</b> (page 307), with doors so heavy only a team of horses can open them. Three hermits, all true disciples of Aratis, guard it and whatever it contains.
PAGE	23
H2	Shrines & temples
HR
P	Aratis has a shrine in Stonetop's pavilion of the gods. Outside of Stonetop: consider whether this community hosts a shrine or temple to Aratis. Small shrines to Aratis might also be found at <b>waysides</b> along the Makers' Roads (page 271), or perhaps at spots where different groups of <b>Hillfolk</b> (page 228) gather and meet.
P	For any given shrine or temple:
Q	Where is it located?
Q	Who tends this place?
Q	How is Aratis herself represented?
Q	What symbols/trappings adorn it?
Q	Which of her <b>themes</b> (previous page) are emphasized?
Q	What high holidays are celebrated here, and how?
Q	What is this shrine or temple like? Perhaps it is… (pick 1)
E	a hub of the community, a place of frequent rites, petitions, and celebrations;
E	used only on high holidays, for each home keeps its own shrine above the hearth;
E	neglected by most, tended only by a handful of true disciples;
E	a grim place of judgement and punishment, shunned by all but her chosen;
E	newly established, cramped and spare;
E	some variation of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
H2	Judges
P	Some communities are home to a Judge of Aratis, who settles disputes, keeps records, and stands guard against agents of chaos.
P	For any given community, consider/ask:
Q	Does a Judge of Aratis reside here?
Q	Who are they? What are they like? What sets them apart?
Q	Has there always been a Judge here? Or is this a recent thing?
Q	How much influence do they hold?
Q	Do they have any apprentices?
Q	How much contact do they have with Judges from other communities?
Q	What is their greatest strength as a Judge? What is their greatest flaw? Maybe pick or roll a theme (previous page) for each.
P	Judges are charged with maintaining a Chronicle, a history of the community they serve, its people, their knowledge, and their traditions. If a community has (or had) a Judge, consider/ask:
Q	How are the records kept?
Q	Where are they? In the Judge's home, a temple, a vault, or what?
Q	How far back do they go?
Q	How well organized are they?
P	Should an NPC Judge (or a communityspanning order of Judges) oppose or cause trouble for the PCs, write them up as a threat (an <i>institution</i>).
P	Remember: NPCs don't have playbooks.
P	An NPC Judge might have tags or moves reminiscent of a PC Judge, or not. See page 25 for some potential NPC Judges.
PAGE	24
H2	True disciples
HR
P	True disciples are those who pledge themselves to Aratis, her principles, and her observances. For any given community, consider/ask:
Q	How many true disciples of Aratis reside here?
Q	Who is most notable among them?
Q	How devout are they, really?
Q	How much influence do they have, as a group?
Q	What contact do they have with disciples from other settlements?
Q	How are they typically chosen? (By birth, by calling, by invitation, etc.)
Q	What rites do they lead/perform, both publicly and in secret?
P	What does Aratis require of her true disciples? The answer might vary from community to community. Perhaps she demands… (pick up to 3)
E	truth, honesty, and forthrightness;
E	hospitality, freely given to all who ask for it;
E	the punishment of thieves & oathbreakers;
E	adherence to strict rules of diet and dress; and/or
E	respect for authority, property, and rank.
P	Should the true disciples of a community oppose or cause trouble for the PCs, write them up as a threat (an <i>institution</i>).

P	• Suss out someone's motives
P	• Keep calm under pressure or scrutiny
P	<b>Circumspect instinct</b> to try to make everyone happy (+<i>friendly</i>, +<i>cautious</i>, deals damage with disadvantage)
P	• Stall, delay, make excuses
P	• See both sides of an issue

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Oathbreaker's curse
P	When you <b><i>swear a proper oath before</i></b> <b><i>a shrine of Aratis</i></b>, in full view of witnesses and with an appropriate offering, you are oathbound. Make note of what you promised, and the nature of the curse you invite should you forswear yourself.
P	When you <b><i>forswear your oath</i></b>, hold 3 Ruin.
P	While you hold Ruin, you have disadvantage whenever you or a companion rolls the Die of Fate.
P	When you <b><i>roll a 10+ on a move</i></b>, you can spend 1 Ruin to turn the 10+ into a 6instead. The GM can refuse; if they do, you retain your Ruin. If they accept, the results should reflect the nature of the curse you invited upon yourself.
H2	Chaos
HR
P	A PC Judge can use their Censure move to denounce another as "an agent of chaos."
P	When they do, the move works regardless of what you think. You can ask questions about their motivations or their thinking, but they're the Judge, not you.
P	With the Hound of Aratis move, the Judge can easily identify things "tainted by chaos," and The Hammer and the Book lets them smite things "of supernatural chaos." The <b>Things Below</b> (page 412) count, as does anything corrupted by them or infused with their power.
P	Beyond that, consider what the Judge has
P	Censured and the doctrine of Aratis that's been established in play. Ask the Judge what they think counts. Consider what you know about the entity in question, and make a ruling. If in doubt, defer to the Die of Fate or the results of a relevant move.
